audit.action: cite a better source for the same coding
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote confirmed verbatim in two held files (web alphabet page lines 101-103; printed Intro PDF p. xvi sec. 1.2). (2) The coding 'fixed final' rests on a 1993 dictionary orthography note, but by the language's principal describers, and it is corroborated by the held Gordon 2002 appendix ('Final', via Rand 1968) and by Hardy 2005 pp. 83-84 as paraphrased second-hand; the held Intro's verb-grade section (pp. xl-xli) independently speaks of 'predictable word-final high tone'. Nothing found suggests the coding is wrong. (3) The record's formal quote/cite/loc/grade fields are empty even though the evidence is held and verified — fill them from the held Intro (p. xvi sec. 1.2, plus pp. xl-xli) and grade accordingly; ideally re-read against Hardy 2005 pp. 83-84 when a copy is obtained. sources.quote: "Otherwise, words are usually accented on the last syllable and since this is predictable, final accent is not written." (Sylestine, Hardy & Montler, Dictionary of the Alabama Language, online edition, "The Alabama alphabet" section; unpaginated web page.) The "otherwise" covers lexically marked pitch accent: "vowels in Alabama may have either a high level tone (written as á, í, or ó) or a high falling tone (written à, ì, or ò)", contrasting e.g. foosi 'bird' with fósi 'grandfather'.
